repo_notes.content: This repository is a simulation-only stack: an autonomous PX4 quadrotor flown in PX4 SITL and Gazebo Harmonic. No real vehicle and no onboard computer has run it; the resource figures are a workstation's (docs/resource_budget.md). Say so on the overview and wherever hardware is discussed. The authoritative source of every requirement, invariant, acceptance rule and number is docs/specification.md: each row is marked as set by the owner or by an agent, and its change log names the commit. Prefer the specification's and the documents' wording and figures to what a structure's field names suggest; when a page describes a configuration structure, give the values the flights run with (drone_city_nav/config/urban_mvp.yaml), not only the field names.
repo_notes.author: Project agent, from docs/specification.md

repo_notes.content: The design invariants (docs/specification.md, rows I1 to I8) are what sets the project apart; state them where they apply and not only on one page. I1: space the sensor has not looked at is traversable at no penalty (no cost, no inflation, no gate); the protection in unknown space is the braking contract, not the map. I2: space is prohibited only by measurement, observed occupied or observed unobservable (the sensor looked and its range stayed short: smoke, darkness, glare); no prohibition comes from configuration, from knowledge of the location or from the vehicle's history. I3: no latch, hold or release gate keyed on the vehicle's history; the vehicle's own position and its observed path are never closed. I4: vertical motion is free in the planner's time model. I5: production code does not adapt to a location (no named world, spawn, opening or passage). I6: safety and the quality of the flight come before speed; a collision is a defect; safety is not bought by a broad reduction of speed. I7: the vehicle does not know how its light will fail; it reads what the light's driver reads. I8: the vehicle has no time limit.
repo_notes.author: Project agent, from docs/specification.md

repo_notes.content: The requirements a flight is judged by (rows R1 to R9): R1 no crash and no contact with any surface (every contact is a crash, analysed and repaired); R2 every goal reached in truth, the true position within the 2.0 m capture radius at the acknowledgement (the truth is read by the check, never by the control loop); R3 the mean flight speed without GNSS, 1.16 m/s on the stereo set and 2.28 m/s on the lidar set; R8 the open-sky profile, 10 m/s at least (measured 10.2); R7 dense smoke is never entered; R9 a survey covers 0.95 of the reachable flyable truth. Nothing else fails a flight (R4). Acceptance is statistical: series of whole flights judged against the simulator's truth (docs/testing.md), five flights a sensor set after every change of flight code.
repo_notes.author: Project agent, from docs/specification.md

repo_notes.content: Key figures to give where the subject comes up. MPPI: 8192 rollouts of 80 steps on the GPU (CUDA, with Vulkan and CPU engines beside it) in 6.4 ms at the median; the planning tick is 20 ms (50 Hz). The braking contract: the speed is bounded so that the vehicle stops inside the range its sensor has actually measured in the frame it brakes on. The default sensor set has no lidar and no GNSS: a forward stereo pair (0.20 m baseline, 120 degrees, depth trusted to 5.2 m), six time-of-flight zone sensors, a thermal core, a carried light; localization is a stereo MSCKF visual-inertial odometry with registration against the vehicle's own map and loop closure. The lidar set uses a 3D lidar (35 m) and lidar-inertial odometry. The obstacle memory is a 0.25 m voxel grid built in flight, with no prior map; the global planner is a persistent, incremental D* Lite on a 3D lattice.
repo_notes.author: Project agent, from docs/specification.md

repo_notes.content: How the project is developed: by coding agents under the owner's rules (docs/autonomous_development.md, docs/goal_writing.md). Decisions are the owner's or an agent's and the specification says which; known gaps are in docs/technical_debt.md with their measured cause; docs/roadmap.md holds the open items and, under 'Completed', the finished ones with their flights. A newcomer's path is docs/guide/01_basics.md to 06_extending.md with docs/guide/architecture_map.md, which links every component to its files and specification rows; reuse that structure.
repo_notes.author: Project agent, from docs/specification.md

page_notes.content: Name every invariant, not only I1. I2 (prohibition only by measurement) and I3 (no gate on the vehicle's history) are the ones other stacks do not hold.

pages.title: Navigation Pipeline
pages.purpose: From sensors to setpoints: depth or lidar returns, the obstacle memory, the distance field, the persistent D* Lite route, the execution supervisor, the MPPI horizon, the offboard setpoints; the topics between the nodes and the 20 ms tick (docs/navigation_pipeline.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/guide/03_mission_and_pipeline.md).

pages.title: Obstacle Memory
pages.purpose: The voxel occupancy memory built in flight with no prior map (docs/obstacle_mapping.md): what makes a voxel occupied or free, the observed-unobservable layer for smoke and darkness, the moving layer for warm bodies, snapshots and deltas, maps persisted from a survey.

page_notes.content: Lead with invariant I1 (unknown space is free and costs nothing) and I2 (a voxel is prohibited only by a measurement). The hit counters are the mechanism, not the idea.

pages.title: Distance Field And Clearance
pages.purpose: The ESDF built from the memory, the body and envelope models, the clearance laws that bound speed near surfaces and the swept-body checks of a horizon.

pages.title: Persistent D* Lite Planner
pages.purpose: The incremental D* Lite on a 3D lattice that keeps its search between replans (docs/replanning.md): the lattice and its edges, the flight-time cost with free vertical motion (I4), repair on a changed world, a goal proven unreachable and the return home.

pages.title: Route Execution And The Braking Contract
pages.purpose: The execution supervisor: horizons certified against the newest world, stops prepared and committed, what happens to a refused stop, and the braking contract that ties speed to the range the sensor measured (docs/drone_control.md, docs/guide/04_safety.md).

page_notes.content: Explain the braking contract in numbers: why the stereo set flies about 1.4 m/s on a depth trusted to 5.2 m and the lidar set about 2.3 m/s, and 10 m/s over the open sky.
page_notes.author: Project agent, from docs/specification.md

pages.title: MPPI Local Planner
pages.purpose: The model predictive path integral controller (docs/trajectory_optimization.md): the cost terms, the horizon, how the route and the distance field enter, the contracts with the execution supervisor.

page_notes.content: Give the figures: 8192 rollouts of 80 steps in 6.4 ms at the median on the GPU inside a 20 ms tick. No other open flying stack reviewed in docs/related_work.md runs MPPI on a GPU.

pages.title: Lidar-Inertial Odometry

pages.purpose: The open sky: the hybrid profile that reads satellite fixes against the estimator's prediction, the faults a relay plays (lost, jammed, spoofed) and how the trust is a measurement with no latch (roadmap item 39, specification K56).
